name: Ossuary Arms Memento Mori OA-3 'Wake'
description:
A bolt-action precision rifle built with a deliberately antiquated aesthetic — walnut stock, blued steel, hand-checkered grip — that conceals a modern BCI-integrated firing computer in its stock. Ossuary Arms builds weapons for operators who believe that the act of precision shooting is a craft, not a procedure.

The Wake's BCI integration is minimal and respectful. It provides wind data, range estimation, and a recommended hold point, but it does not guide the round or correct for shooter error. The operator must still execute the shot. Ossuary's founder has been quoted saying 'The machine tells you where to aim. Your hands decide if you are worthy.'

The Memento Mori fires a heavy 10.3mm match round at subsonic velocities through a hand-fitted barrel that achieves sub-MOA accuracy at 1,000 meters. Each rifle is engraved with the name of its first owner and cannot be re-registered.
legality: Licensed — registered to named individual only
specifications:
caliber: 10.3mm match-grade subsonic
effective_range: 100-1,200 meters
rate_of_fire: Bolt-action, 1 round per 5 seconds
capacity: 3-round internal magazine
weight: 5.6 kg
power_source: BCI computer: micro-cell, 200 hours standby
tactical_use: The Wake is not a battlefield weapon. It is deployed by operators who select their engagements carefully and value precision over volume. The heavy subsonic round delivers devastating terminal performance while maintaining a suppressed acoustic signature. Operators who carry the Memento Mori tend to work alone, take single engagements, and disappear. The weapon's registered nature means that every Wake kill can theoretically be traced — operators accept this as part of the weapon's philosophy of accountability.
cultural_context: Ossuary Arms has become a cult brand among precision shooters who reject the automation trend in modern weaponry. Owning a Wake is a statement about craftsmanship, accountability, and the belief that killing should require skill rather than technology. The engraving tradition means that a Wake carries its owner's name into every engagement — a permanent record of who chose to pull the trigger.
story_hooks: A Wake engraved with a dead operator's name has surfaced on the black market. Ossuary's policy prohibits re-registration, meaning whoever uses it carries a dead person's identity into every engagement.

Ossuary Arms' founder has been diagnosed with a terminal illness and is building one final rifle — a masterwork Wake that they intend to auction. The anticipated bidding war has attracted attention from people who want the weapon for more than its craftsmanship.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately retro precision rifle with classical hunting-rifle aesthetics — graceful walnut furniture and blued steel barrel married to a subtly modern stock that houses concealed electronics. The silhouette reads pre-2100s craftsmanship at first glance, but close inspection reveals micro-seams and the faint luminescence of a dormant BCI interface beneath the checkered grip.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 118 cm | Barrel length: 61 cm | Stock depth: 8.5 cm | Width at receiver: 5.2 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and deliberate — 5.6 kg feels substantial in hand without being unwieldy. The weight distribution favors the receiver, making the rifle feel grounded and intentional. Not a weapon you carry casually.
physical_description.primary_material: Walnut hardwood stock (hand-finished), blued 4340 chrome-moly steel receiver and barrel, polymer BCI housing (concealed within stock), carbon-fiber internal reinforcement
physical_description.finish: Blued steel with deliberate micro-patina (aged without being neglected). Walnut stock has a satin oil finish with visible wood grain. Hand-checkering on grip shows subtle tool marks indicating craft rather than CNC precision. Stock interior seams reveal brushed titanium BCI casing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep blued-black steel, warm medium walnut brown with honey undertones, gunmetal gray BCI housing (barely visible), brass scope mounts and trigger guard
physical_description.grip_texture: Hand-checkered walnut with diamond cross-pattern — slightly raised texture provides secure grip without aggressive aggressive abrasion. Feels like traditional guncraft. Hidden beneath: subtle tactile feedback nodes from BCI interface (detectable only to augmented users).
distinctive_features: Hand-fitted bolt with polished locking lugs
Concealed BCI firing computer beneath stock checkering — visible only as faint geometric seams
Engraved owner name on receiver (permanent registration marker)
Muzzle brake designed for subsonic round signature management
Scope rail mounted on receiver (typically equipped with variable optics)
Heavy, precisely-machined action with minimal rattle
Brass cartridge elevator and ejector port with minimalist design
Unique per-rifle serial number alongside owner's name
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: OSSUARY ARMS engraved in serif font on left side of receiver. Maker's mark (stylized memento mori skull within circle) stamped above trigger guard. Individual operator's registered name engraved in italic script on right side of receiver — this marking is permanent and unique per rifle.
physical_description.condition_typical: Paradoxically both pristine and weathered. The walnut and steel show meticulous maintenance and light field wear — minor handling marks, subtle salt-corrosion patina on exposed steel (indicating field deployment), and microscopic dust in checkering. Operators maintain these weapons obsessively; they carry history but no abuse.
